courses.title: Select many: the kinds of selection that make sense
courses.objective: One panel lists every selection that is possible for what you picked — coplanar, parallel, same-area, same-radius faces; parallel and same-length edges; all bodies — each with a count, applied all at once or ‘1 by 1’.

steps.title: Build the part
instructions: A plate with a hole is built.
steps.why: You need faces and edges to select.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: Open Select many
instructions: Click a face, then Select many (the bar, AakarFORM › Pick, or Alt+Q).
The panel lists only choices that apply to a face, each with how many it would select.
steps.why: Choices with 0 results are greyed out, so you never click something that does nothing.

checkpoint.expected: The Select many panel is open.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: New · Add · Remove
instructions: Choose Parallel faces: the top and bottom are selected.
Switch to Add, pick Same radius to add the hole wall; switch to Remove, pick Coplanar to take the top away again.
steps.why: The mode decides how a choice combines with the current selection.

checkpoint.expected: The selection changes with each mode.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: Edges
instructions: Click an edge: the panel now offers Parallel edges, Same length, Tangent chain, Loop of a face, All sharp edges.
steps.why: The list changes with the kind of thing selected.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: Faces looking…
instructions: Use the ‘Faces looking…’ chips (+Z, −Z, +X …) to select every face that faces that way.
steps.why: Fast way to pick all the tops or all the sides.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.
